articleTitle: A New Remote System for Monitoring Physiological Parameters of Elderly People
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, a new remote system for monitoring physiological parameters of elderly people is presented. The proposed patient monitoring system consists of a Fitbit Sense device, a smartphone that runs on the Android operating system, and a cloud-based infrastructure. The Fitbit Sense device runs a custom developed application that collects in the real-time physiological signal data, including heart rate, skin temperature, oxygen saturation and other parameters, and communicates with the smartphone companion solely through Bluetooth connectivity. The smartphone companion application then transmits this data to the cloud-based platform via cellular communication network or WiFi network. A remote patient monitoring application is running in cloud due to the flexibility and scalability offered by cloud computing services. With this solution, medical staff can configure device settings, receive timely notifications, and respond promptly to patient health issues without requiring on-site personnel. Additionally, medical staff or caretaker can remotely send personalized notifications and alerts directly to the Fitbit Sense device, enabling patients to take proactive control of their health.

articleTitle: Linearity Evaluation and Influence of the Reference Voltage for ADC Converter of Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the problems related to an existing ADC converter. The study contains measurements, experiments and comparison between two same modules for which we try to highlight the problems of that converter. The analog-to-digital converter used in the present application is integrated in the ESP32 board. The first problem would be related to the low linearity compared to other dedicated ADCs. For this was used a signal generator and a table values generator with which was generated a linear voltage and data analysis software for statistical results. Another problem is related to the reference voltage for which we observe differences between board to another boards. The conclusions of this study provide us with valuable information about the use of a converter, giving us solutions for optimizing the acquisition of an analogic signal.

articleTitle: Addressing the Skills Gap in Microelectronics — Development and Validation of Reactive Response in the Project European Chips Skills Academy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The European Chips Skills Academy (ECSA), funded by the European Union, began in October 2023 to address the skills and workforce gap in the microelectronics sector. Work Package 5 (WP5) focuses on creating specialised training content for the ECSA, targeting the current and future workforce in Europe’s electronics and microelectronics industries. Initially, WP5 is producing training materials on soft skills, such as agile management and digital competences, to support remote workforce development in response to COVID19. Later, the project will expand to include curricula on digital skills, entrepreneurship, green initiatives, and specific microelectronics topics. The developed content will be tested and validated through a Test and Validation Plan, which details activities, timelines, and feedback tools. This plan ensures standardised training and visiting activities, along with uniform reporting by partners, facilitating the final Validation Report and recommendations for improving ECSA training.

articleTitle: Development of an Electronic Monitoring System for a Savonius Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Wind energy stands as a significant renewable resource, particularly in the European Union, where it holds the primary position among renewable energy sources, followed by hydropower and solar photovoltaics [1]. Forecasts indicate that by 2028, wind and solar energy together will constitute a significant 96% share of renewable electricity capacity [2]. This paper investigates the development of an electronic monitoring system for a Savonius vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) designed for low-wind energy areas, based on our previous research [3]. The design and implementation of an embedded electronic monitoring system specifically for this type of wind turbine are discussed. The integration of the wind turbine with the monitoring system enables real-time tracking and analysis of key performance parameters, such as output power, turbine speed, and generator voltage, which are systematically recorded in an online database. This approach not only improves the operational efficiency and reliability of the wind turbine but also offers a scalable solution for remote monitoring and data management in renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: PCB temperature controller for automated soldering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents the design and layout of a PCB that implements a closed-loop temperature control system for automated soldering. The PID control algorithm can adjust the power delivered to a heating element represented by a meander copper track embedded in the PCB using feedback from a thermocouple. This enables the system to follow the thermal profile of the solder paste, ensuring optimal results with no soldering skills required from the user. The end product resembles a commercial hot-plate but is also equipped with a connector for PCBs with a segmented copper plane on layer 2 as a heating element, creating self-soldering PCBs.

articleTitle: Monitoring System with Autonomous Power Supply and Remote Radio Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A comprehensive monitoring system has been developed that is capable of measuring and recording critical environmental parameters, such as air and soil temperature, humidity, dust particle concentration and light flux. The system uses LoraWAN to send the collected data to a dedicated application that provides the user with real-time information to make informed decisions. A key objective was to develop a powerful, flexible, cost-effective system that integrates multiple environmental sensors with advanced communication and power management systems and ensures robust and autonomous operation so that the system can be deployed in different environments depending on the user’s needs.

articleTitle: The Intelligent Cover for Comfort and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The medical device can monitor the subject with different problems in the house. People who spend time in the chair can develop a column illness. The body posture on the chair is important to prevent column deviation. This paper presents a system that can identify the body posture and the time spent on the chair. Flex sensors are plotted on the mattress to identify body pressure on the chair. The data are read on an SD card and laptop to be analyzed in PYTHON. The circuit is simulated in PROTEUS software before real implementation. After the data classification using machine learning algorithms, a 98% accuracy is obtained.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a low-cost modular electronic system for home automation based on IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: IoT-based home automation systems are gaining increasing popularity. Research shows that relatively few households effectively utilize such systems. This article presents the development of an inexpensive, multifunctional, and reliable smart home solution using Arduino and Raspberry Pi microcomputers. The constructed system is modular to provide a universal solution. The main component of the module (AM) is the Arduino microprocessor, which, with its analog and digital inputs and outputs, allows for the connection of multiple sensors and actuators for measuring and controlling various parameters. To expand the managed processes within the household, multiple modules can be used. Raspberry Pi serves as the server for processing and visualizing data. System configuration, management, and analysis are handled through a graphical user interface (GUI). The user can set values for the controlled parameters as well as select from different scenarios. Communication between the microcontrollers is established via a wireless TCP/IP network protocol. Data is recorded in a database, allowing for long-term storage and analysis. The developed system simplifies the operation of smart devices used in the household and enables the optimization of various domestic processes, including energy consumption, security, comfort, and more.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Temperature Monitoring System for the Safety of Electric Vehicle Transport on Maritime Transport
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a practical application for a growing technology: the Internet of Things (IoT). It details the design and implementation of a custom, battery-powered, embedded prototype system for fast and early fire detection in vehicles onboard maritime transport. The system primarily relies on gas detection and thermal imaging cameras. The system utilizes a network of portable sensors mounted underneath the vehicles for monitoring. These sensors communicate with a central base station using the LoRa protocol for long-range, low-power communication. Prior to installation, each sensor is programmed using an integrated keyboard to specify its exact mounting location. The base station then interrogates each sensor individually, receiving real-time data only from the queried sensor. This data includes the location, CO and COV concentrations, ambient temperature and humidity, and the temperature beneath the vehicle surface. The base station acts as a server with integrated Wi -Fi and Bluetooth for wireless communication. This allows for easy access to the collected data in the future from a mobile application, website, or online database. The data is displayed on a web interface for convenient monitoring and analysis. Additionally, both the base station and the web interface display visual alerts. To ensure quicker detection and response, an audio signal also sounds from the sensor that detects the danger.

articleTitle: TIE M CAD Design Challenge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The TIE M-Mechanical CAD Design Challenge is a competitive event designed to assess the proficiency of mechanical engineering students in computer-aided design (CAD). With a specific focus on electronic packaging and electro-mechanical assembly, this challenge evaluates the students’ capabilities in designing and manufacturing mechanical components using advanced CAD software. Through this challenge, students demonstrate their technical knowledge and skills acquired through coursework, positioning the challenge as a benchmark certification in mechanical CAD design within the realm of electronic systems.

articleTitle: Smart Solutions for Sustainable Urban and Food System Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper investigates innovative ways of testing and quality control in urban growth and sustainable food production. These programs are aimed at solving important environmental and health challenges through the encouragement of urban gardening as well as the conversion of food loss and waste into valuable plant-based proteins. The IPSUS initiative is developing new techniques for extracting proteins from potatoes, brewers’ spent grain, and seaweeds. To foster sustainable urban expansion, U-GARDEN incorporates city planning with urban gardens that have numerous advantages such as greater community participation, improved environmental health care and more home-grown food supplies. Integrating IoT systems is a key element in enhancing management as well as monitoring these sustainable activities. Grafana platform helps in visualizing temperature information gathered by these sensors alongside humidity levels plus energy consumption they measure within the system. The real-time visualization dashboard provided by Grafana enables researchers and stakeholders to monitor the quality of the upcycling processes. To facilitate the strategic planning and management of urban gardens a multi-criteria tool has been developed within the U-GARDEN project. To determine the best places for urban gardens, this tool incorporates sociodemographic characteristics. This article highlights the potential for major environmental, social, and health advantages by including creative ways to upcycle FLW and encourage urban gardening.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Assessment of Hydration Status Using Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper investigates a detailed experiment measuring human body impedance to assess hydration status. The primary goal of the study is to develop a non-invasive method for monitoring hydration through body impedance analysis and to demonstrate the practical applicability of this method in the biomedical field. The experiment integrates a prototype using the XR2206 function generator, LM324 operational amplifier, and Arduino Nano to capture and analyze impedance variations. The focus was on capturing impedance variations using strategically placed electrodes. The results show a clear correlation between hydration levels and body impedance, supporting the potential of this method for hydration status evaluation.

articleTitle: Industrial Greenhouse Monitoring and Forecasting System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, the way to create and implement a system that uses machine learning elements to monitor environmental conditions in a greenhouse is presented. The system includes a sensor block, a control block and a power block. The hardware component includes light, humidity and temperature sensors, Li-Ion battery and a special USB charging circuit. The Raspberry Pi system manages all these functions, and the data collected by the sensors will be taken by the system and stored in a database. The data will then be used to train an algorithm based on automatic learning for the automatic adjustments of the greenhouse. Therefore, the greenhouse can be controlled automatically, and the user will be notified by a remote e-mail alert system if certain limits are exceeded.

articleTitle: Technologies of Interconnections in Electronics – Signal and Power Integrity Student Contest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Signal and Power integrity topics are of great importance in the current evolution of digital circuits. The innovations in the integrated circuit manufacturing process (i.e. smaller and faster switching transistors) and the new signal coding (e.g. Pulse Amplitude Modulation 4) allowed the industry to achieve new high digital speeds. However, this puts a lot of pressure on high-speed design when planning the stack-up, designing/placing the vias and managing the routing traces losses. As a result, the industry needs engineers with knowledge and skills to address the new challenges in emergent digital high-speed design. The university curriculum addresses some of the topics, but most of the time from a theoretical point of view. Through the collaboration between universities and industry, a student contest was created that has as purpose to address industry challenges. The students have the chance to apply what they learned during the university curriculum but are also acquiring new knowledge through the advanced training that takes place during the contest. The purpose is to build engineers with knowledge in high-speed digital design.

articleTitle: Application of IoT Technologies as a University Project for Students: Challenges and Possibilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Practical projects are crucial in university curriculums, allowing students to research, develop, and present projects, thus demonstrating their knowledge and skills. This paper describes a complex project suitable for students’ practical internships that could evolve into a comprehensive thesis by their fourth year. The project consists of assembling a soil parameter measuring station, and integrating knowledge from disciplines about hardware, electronics, programming, networking, operating systems, databases, and information systems. The requirements include selecting suitable software technologies, programming microcontrollers, choosing network protocols and databases, and developing data handling and visualization tools.Challenges include defining project requirements, managing student expectations for detailed guidance, and navigating research on new technologies. This publication details the project’s development stages, issues encountered, and the evolution of both the students’ approaches and the counselors’ strategies over nearly three years.

articleTitle: Implementing Boolean Four-Input Functions with Multiplexers When Applying Project-Based Learning in the Digital Electronics Course
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents the application of innovative teaching methods, such as project-based learning, in the course “Digital Electronics” for students-bachelors at the University of Ruse for implementing Boolean functions of four arguments, widely used in practice, with 8-input and 4-input multiplexers with additional logic gates.

articleTitle: Web Platform for Designing a Hydropower System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative solution to design and create a web platform that contains two applications: one that allows users to design a hydropower system with the help of some basic elements, and the other that allows monitoring the flow of a pipeline. Based on the practical results obtained with the help of the two applications, it can be observed that the created web platform offers results according to the real-life parameters.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Dielectric Tests of PLA/Flax Sustainable and Degradable PCB Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: To pursue a move towards sustainability in electronics manufacturing, recently we presented a biodegradable printed circuit board (PCB) alternative substrate, where polylactic-acid (PLA) and flax-textile reinforcement forms a composite with flame retardancy. The novel PLA/Flax substrate is capable of being a core material for double-sided PCB designs. This paper investigates into the lowfrequency ($1 \mathrm{~Hz}-500 \mathrm{kHz}$) dielectric capabilities of the substrates with Omicron Dirana dielectric spectrometer and Wayne-Kerr 6430A impedance analyzer. For the experimental, two generations of one-sided substrates were measured, where the top side was covered with $35 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ Cu layer with PLA foil and polypropylene (PP) foil (A and B groups consequentially) serving as bonding layer between the composite and the Cu. It was found that The PLA/Flax substrates have high permittivity values at low frequencies, while at high frequencies, the permittivity is lower than that of the most commonly used FR4. Moreover, the additional PP layer caused a further increase in the relative permittivity. The tan $\delta$ of PLA/PLA samples was higher over the investigated frequency range. This high value of relative permittivity and dielectric loss at low frequency is connected to interfacial polarization originated from the structure of PLA/Flax samples. A local peak of $\tan \delta$ was observed at 500 Hz on PLA/Flax samples indicating the presence of orientation polarization.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Analysis and Channel Reach Extension for a PCIe 3.0 Digital Interface using CST Studio and Altium Designer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative methodology for evaluating signal integrity in PCIe Gen 3 systems by extending the transmission path through the integration of an extension board. A systematic workflow is presented, encompassing both simulation and measurement techniques, to guarantee robust high-speed data transmission. The findings offer critical insights and practical recommendations for engineers engaged in similar applications, with a primary focus on preserving signal integrity in next-generation PCIe interfaces.

articleTitle: Investigating the Copper Peel and Solder Joint Shear Strength on Biodegradable Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The amount of electronics waste is increasing rapidly, and replacing traditional electronics materials with biodegradable alternatives is essential where possible. Four types of biodegradable substrates with $35 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ thick laminated copper layer have been analysed in this research work. All the substrates are based on polylactic acid laminates with flax reinforcement. The first type is a pure PLA laminate. The second, third and fourth types incorporate polymer interlayers (polypropylene or polyamide) to facilitate the adhesion between the copper layer and the substrate. Note that the interlayers are not biodegradable but will be swapped with biodegradable alternatives in the future. Copper peel strength was measured using a standard test pattern described in IPC-TM650. The copper layers were peeled off using an Instron 5965 test equipment, and the applied load was recorded automatically. A custom sliding sample holder was designed, allowing the vertical peeling of the copper layer. In addition to the copper peeling test, surface-mounted resistors in different sizes were assembled with low-temperature reflow soldering, and the shear strength of their solder joints was investigated.

articleTitle: Research for the Realization and Testing of an Adaptive, Programmable Dosing System for Hydro Electrolytic Balancing (SDAEH)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This work presents an adaptive-programmable system based on an infusion pump for hydro electrolytic dosing in the case of specialized interventions (emergency services) in environmental climatic conditions $\left(-20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}+40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$, performance tests and properties functions of the SDAEH system under laboratory or car transport conditions. Functional parameter testing was done in accordance with the European techniques set out in BS EN 60601-2-24:1998, taking into account different variants where appropriate. For each test, a new administration set was used in accordance with the environmental and climatic conditions. The parameters specific to infusion pumps, such as: constant index, process recovery time, pump bolus size, pump negative bolus size, are new concepts and are variants proposed by the IEC 60601-2-24 standard. Algorithms used for their calculation can be modified by existing specialized staff. For all tests, only one pump and a limited number of disposable accessories were tested. The results are a measure of the performance of a single pump. They cannot be assumed by other devices or the same type of pump even if they have identical functionality. A new set of re-administration devices should be used for each test. During this stage, a series of performance tests and functional properties of the SDAEH system were performed in laboratory conditions using the existing electronic equipment.

articleTitle: Conceptual Model of a Parking System with Automatic License Plate Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Automating the process of managing the entrance and exit in parking lots is particularly important not only from a scientific point of view, but also in order to facilitate our everyday life. This paper describes our proposed conceptual model of a parking system based on a Raspberry Pi microcomputer and algorithms for automatic license plate text recognition. The individual modules of the system are described in detail, along with their functions, and an algorithm of the model’s operation is proposed and described. For the implementation of a test prototype, infrared sensors were used for the entrance and exit, which, when a car is detected, transmit a signal to the raspberi pie module. It activates a camera that captures an image of the front of the car. The Python implemented software part of the system receives this image and, after preprocessing, returns the recognized registration number as text. This text, together with other information forms a record in a relational database. To improve the performance of the system, it would be good to add to recognition of the text from the registration plate also recognition of the make, model, type and color of the car.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric Behavior Simulation in Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In the electronics industry, there are currently many circuit simulators based on PSPICE that solve the system of equations resulting from the application of Kirchhoff’s two theorems (for voltages and currents) for all circuit nodes and all circuit loops, respectively [1]. A major disadvantage of these simulators is that they cannot use components where electrical parameters change depending on other non-electrical parameters, such as temperature or something else. One such device is the thermistor, whose electrical resistance changes non-linearly with temperature. Current solutions offered by PSPICE simulators consist of modeling with ABM blocks the characteristics of the components, where the input variable is a temperature value. This paper proposes the use of a simulator that allows for the addition of non-electrical components. The paper describes the design steps and highlights, comparatively, the advantages of including the thermo-electric components directly in the simulator compared to the currently used PSPICE simulators that contain only electrical components. The paper emphasizes the advantages obtained in the educational process; the authors highlight the fact that by using these new simulators, students can understand much more easily how the entire system works and the correct way of designing automatic systems.

articleTitle: EMI numerical simulations and measurements of spread spectrum frequency modulation by an automotive boost LED driver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: CISPR25:2021 is the standard responsible for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of LED automotive drivers. One method for reducing of conducted emissions (CE) produced by DC-DC converter is gate signal spread spectrum frequency modulation (SSFM). This paper presents a SSFM study consist of PSpice Simulations of CISPR25:2021 measurement and the result of CE measurements according to CISPR25:2021.

articleTitle: Remote controlled automatic test bench
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a solution for creating a remotely controlled test stand for testing electronic modules. The architecture of the stand and the method of interconnection of the component instruments are indicated. The implementation of the user interface and the semi-automatic / automatic test sequences is based on the Python language and the graphic interfaces specific to each tool. The results of running the test sequences are available in structured reports.

articleTitle: Comparative Workbench Study about MTBF for PoL Buck-Converters: Asynchronous vs. Synchronous
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The advantages and disadvantages of the two types of buck converters are well known. Considering that the latter has prevailed in electronic practice, when it comes to PoL converters, the problem arises of investigating which of the two is more reliable (comparing them keeping the equivalent footprint, volumetric power density per square inch, and with equal electrical parameters). The paper systematically and rigorously addresses the problem of the reliability of both type of converters using the capture of the temperature of the devices in the IR and based on it calculating the MTBF using the latest international standard, namely IEC 61709 (released 2017). The components’ environmental conditions were defined by a standard buck converter. The results were compared by taking account of component’s temperature and application of specific concepts like references conditions and operating conditions.

articleTitle: Development of Control Strategies for an Industrial Robot to Increase Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper aims to optimize the energy consumption of industrial robots, with the goal of reducing operational costs and improving the sustainability of the production process. The methods discussed include using energy-efficient components, reducing idle times, and optimizing robot trajectory programming to minimize unnecessary movements. The project presents a simulation of an industrial process for sorting and depalletizing parts using a KUKA KR 4 Agilus robot, along with Arduino development boards for control and coordination. A color sensor system is employed for object detection, optimizing the robot’s movements based on the data collected. To analyze energy and time efficiency, two movement routines were compared: one based on SLIN and the other on SPTP.

articleTitle: Understanding Electrochemical Migration Behavior in Fe2O3-Enhanced SAC Lead-Free Alloys
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The effect of ferric oxide $\left(\mathrm{Fe}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}\right)$ nanoparticle incorporation on the reliability of SAC305 solder alloy, in terms of electrochemical migration (ECM) behavior, was studied using water drop (WD) tests performed in a $0.1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}$ solution with a 10 VDC. The incorporation of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles at different weight percentages ($\mathbf{0. 1 \%}$ and 0.25%) into SAC305, referred to as nanocomposite SAC305-x $(0.1,0.25$ wt. $\% \mathrm{Fe}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$), resulted in a significant shorter mean time to failure (MTTF) compared to pure SAC305. This result indicates that the SAC305 alloy with incorporated Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles exhibits lower ECM resistance than undoped SAC305. A comprehensive surface analysis was conducted on the dendrites formed during the WD test for nanocomposite solders in various solutions, including $0.1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}, 10 \mathrm{mM} \mathrm{H} \mathrm{O}_{2}, 10 \mathrm{mM} \mathrm{HCl}$, and $10 \mathrm{mM} \mathrm{HNO}_{3}$. In all cases, the dendrite morphology predominantly displayed straight, perpendicular branching, resembling a fishbone-like structure. Elemental composition analysis consistently identified Sn as the dominant element in the dendrites, indicating that the ECM behavior of the nanocomposite solders is still primarily governed by the dissolution of Sn.

articleTitle: A Reference Architecture for Deploying Large Language Model Applications in Industrial Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into industrial environments presents numerous challenges. Firstly, understanding the term LLM, its required components for implementation, and the various types of LLMs demands research effort. Furthermore, the processing of textual data involves enormous data volumes, and executing large language models requires substantial computational power. A significant challenge in model deployment on the shopfloor is the stringent data security measures, which often prohibit direct internet access to the cloud.To address these challenges, a reference architecture was developed to give an overview of the components for integrating LLM applications in industry. This architecture covers all essential steps of LLM applications, including data preparation, model training, model evaluation, model deployment, and prompt engineering. For model deployment, two possible locations were distinguished: the digital workplace, such as the office, and the shopfloor. In addition to model deployment, data preparation and model evaluation are emphasized as critical elements for the success of Large Language Model Operations (LLMOps) applications.This reference architecture enables project teams to better understand the elements involved in the LLM integration process. Furthermore, the universal approach helps in standardizing the associated processes, facilitating a more effective acceptance of LLMs in industrial environments.

articleTitle: Optimizations of the Packaging of Li-Ion Battery Packs for Increasing Preconditioning Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper analyzes the effect the packaging of LiIon battery packs has on the efficiency of preconditioning. Then approaches to negating the detrimental effects of the packaging to the effectiveness of preconditioning are analyzed. Different materials and heat transfer media are analyzed to make recommendations that can lead to eliminating this negative effect and even gain in preconditioning efficiency.

articleTitle: A Cloud Computing Solution for Quality Management Systems in Multi-Site Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The solution presented in this paper is an implementation based on cloud computing services for quality management systems. Thus, an architecture of the solution proposed by us will be presented, a presentation of the hardware resources and the mode of operation and finally a presentation of the results of the implementation of the proposed Quality Management System Cloud Computing (QMSCC) structure in the field of the car manufacturing industry. The novelty elements proposed in the paper are represented by the implementation of a cloud computing structure for solving QMS problems in an enterprise with more sites distributed in several regions.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Active Balancing Types for Lithium-Ion Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Battery Management System (BMS) of electric vehicles plays a crucial role in efficient energy management. The BMS is responsible for monitoring the voltage of each cell, the temperature of each cell, the current through each cell, and can send commands for cooling or heating systems. It determines the state of health of the cell and the state of aging. One of the most important functions of a BMS is cell balancing. Ideally, each component cell of the battery pack would have the same capacity, the same voltage, the same internal resistance, and the same rate of aging. However, this scenario is idealistic; in reality, small differences between cells arise during the manufacturing process, leading to considerable imbalances between cells. This paper aims to comparatively study the efficiency of different active balancing types that utilize either capacitors, inductors, or converters. To illustrate the differences between the various balancing methods, balancing circuits were created in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Solar Powered Raspberry Pi for Internet of Things and Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper follows the design, development and later testing of a solar powered Raspberry Pi for Internet of Things (IoT) and wireless sensor networks for environmental sensing, specifically for high spatial resolution irradiance ground measurements. The problem of solar irradiance intermittency can be addressed using either high orbit remote sensing (i.e., satellite imagery), or either using a network of ground stations for observations and measurements. The latter being the more accessible in terms of cost, the paper will tackle developing and testing a single node of such a network. Being a solar powered node, the aim will be to have the network autonomous in terms of energy. This single node ground station has environmental sensors for temperature and irradiance measurements and a camera connected to it for cloud optical flow estimations. The meteorological profile of the site where the device is installed demands an energy consumption scheduler used to turn on or off various modules of the node, depending on the available battery level and the solar resource to keep the measurements integrity at a high level. The node can act as a standalone Internet of things multiprotocol gateway considering that all the primary ways of connectivity are available (cellular, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth).

articleTitle: Considerations regarding environmental testing of a solderless assembly for electronics module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Among the solderless assembly for electronics, additive manufacturing is already applicable in the electronics industry, but to an extent too small compared to its potential. The advancement of this innovative technology is largely dependent on demonstrating the promised higher reliability of the resulting electronic product. Therefore, technology challenges must be identified through simulations and experiments and remedial solutions must be found. In one approach, epoxy resins are used to create a rigid structure with embedded electronic components layer by layer. Here, the interface between the resin layers could be a major vulnerability. The paper presents the experimental investigation of the behaviour of the interface in the case of temperature variations and is mainly focused on an accelerated test at extreme temperature variations by two-fluid-bath method. Following the thermal shock cycles, air penetration was observed at the interface between the layers.

articleTitle: Power Integrity Analysis of a Power Line Between a DDR4 Memory and a Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Power integrity (PI) is a highly debated topic in the electronics industry as it can exhibit a substantial range of problems, each with its unique causes and solutions. The field of PI encompasses everything from voltage regulator modules to on-die capacitance and on-die core power rails. In this paper, an analysis on PI of a power rail by running DC drop and decoupling simulations using the HyperLynx was performed. Using this tool, the placement and size of the decoupling capacitors was performed. The DC drop simulations for different board temperatures were done to obtain all the DC drop characteristics of the proposed design. For the decoupling simulation the impedance properties of the designed power rail referencing a predetermined target impedance were obtained.

articleTitle: Flexible Supercapacitors for Energy Supply in Smart Textiles – Applications and Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Smart textiles and wearable products have recently become popular, however some drawbacks such as the energy supply with heavy batteries still hinders mass production of such textile products. In order to overpass this drawback, flexible supercapacitors represent a promising alternative for energy supply and also have outstanding properties regarding power density, resistance to many charge-discharge cycles and resistance to a wide temperature range. In this work we propose the manufacturing of a flexible supercapacitor prototype, meant to be integrated into a smart textile product for energy supply of its electronic components. The supercapacitor was made of two Nickel electrodes, one separator acting also as electrolyte and two connectors. The measurement of its electrical parameters, namely electric conductivity of the electrodes ($250 \mathrm{~S} / \mathrm{m}$), equivalent series resistance ($6.9 \Omega$) and electrical capacitance (8.64 F) of the assembled supercapacitor yielded promising results, to be further developed and optimized.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Algorithms on Synthetic Lithium-ion Cell Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The proposed paper presents a comprehensive comparative study of various Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning algorithms applied to synthetic data of Lithium-Ion cell. This study utilizes complex datasets generated using a detailed battery cell model, simulating both charging and discharging processes using MATLAB ${ }^{\text {TM }}$. Once generated, the data is subsequently loaded into NI SystemLink ${ }^{\mathrm{TM}}$ Enterprise, where it is processed and analyzed using the Jupyter Notebook feature. Multiple AI/ML models are trained and evaluated on this data, with their performances being compared based on key metrics such as prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to determine the most effective algorithms for this application.

articleTitle: Integrating photovoltaic systems into HVAC control using fuzzy algorithms for optimizing thermal comfort
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This article presents a study on the use of photovoltaic panels for storing electrical energy intended to power an HVAC unit placed in a residential room. To highlight this aspect, two specific scenarios will be considered. Thus, we aim to analyze whether the generated and stored energy is sufficient to fulfil the thermal comfort requirements of the user, while also considering the primary objective of minimizing energy consumption. To achieve this goal, the HVAC unit will be controlled by implementing a fuzzy system that determines its optimal activation based on the comfort level obtained from the user. The fuzzy system presents as inputs both environmental parameters and specific personal perception parameters of the user. The research results provide an insight into the efficiency of implementing photovoltaic energy storage systems for residential applications and propose solutions for optimizing energy consumption in the context of ensuring adequate thermal comfort. Thus, the study contributes to the development of sustainable and personalized energy solutions for smart homes.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Identification with the Application of Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: For predictive maintenance, it is very important to be able to make predictions as well as possible to avoid stopping the production lines. Thus, we started taking the data provided by the vibration and temperature sensors and with the help of the Kalman filter, we achieved a much clearer trend of bearing wear in the measured systems by eliminating the noises. The Kalman filter is an estimator, a “state estimator” for systems that can be modeled by the linear quadratic problem. This is defined as a problem in estimating the instantaneous state of a linear dynamic system perturbed by white noise. The Kalman filter is also used to predict the probable future course of dynamic systems where there is little chance they will be regulated, such as the course of a river during a flood or the trajectory of a celestial body. In this paper, approached an analysis of vibration signals using the Kalman filter, and after obtaining the data from the vibration sensor, we applied the filter and obtained a better prediction of the signals.

articleTitle: DeFraudify4ALL: Prototyping and Validation of a System for Fraud Detection with Big Data and Cloud Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents the prototyping and validation of a Financial Data Management and Analysis System designed to enhance fraud detection using advanced Big Data and Cloud technologies. The system incorporates a Java-based worker for data retrieval and analysis from various sources, including external APIs. The processed data is efficiently stored in a Data Lake utilizing Dremio, Apache Arrow, and Apache Parquet technologies. By leveraging cloud platforms such as AWS, the system ensures scalability, security, and flexibility. Additionally, the integration of sophisticated data visualization tools and AI algorithms, particularly Random Forest, enhances the system’s ability to detect fraudulent activities.

articleTitle: Intelligent System for Investigating the Effects of the Environment on the Human Brain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an intelligent system designed to investigate the effects of environmental conditions on human brain activity. Using the NeuroSky MindSet EEG headset and LucidScribe software, the system measures brain waves (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Theta, and Delta) under different conditions such as calm, stress, and noise. Additional factors like sleep quality, physical activity, and alcohol consumption were controlled using smart devices to ensure reliable results. The results demonstrate significant variations in brain wave activity under different stimuli, with potential applications in educational, psychological, and cognitive ergonomics.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Shielding Fabrics with Antimicrobial Properties for Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Flexible textile shields for electromagnetic radiation protection were made possible with the progress of metallic threads spinning and with the progress of textile manufacturing technologies. The scientific contributions on this topic are widespread and in the last decade additional textile-specific properties were rendered to the flexible shields, such as: fireproofing, hydrophobic, oleophobic, antimicrobial, breathability etc. Our current research is focused on the investigation of the anti-microbial character of electromagnetic shielding woven fabrics with inserted silver and stainless steel threads. The fabrics are meant to be used for healthcare protection as covers against non-ionizing radiation. The antimicrobial activity of these textile shields was investigated by three strains of pahtologic fungi: Candida albicans, Trichoderma viride and Aspergillus niger. The materials were investigated following a modified ASTM G21-15 method and percent reduction rates were calculated, compared to a $\mathbf{100 \%}$ cotton test fabric without silver content.

articleTitle: A Qualitative Inquiry into Student Competitions in Electronics in Romania
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: National student competitions, especially in electronics, are a relatively new area of education. Competitions have been proven to boost engagement, skill development and improve retention. This process, if done correctly, also provides students and learners alike with the skills and information needed to succeed in various areas of electronics design. This paper will focus on the student competition, Technologies of Interconnections in Electronics (TIE), and its proposed benefits towards students in the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) design domain. The performed study was conducted using qualitative methods, as these provide deeper insight into the perceived benefits students gain from participating in such a competition. For the qualitative research approach, the ethnography research method was chosen, as this method provides information through the eyes of someone involved in the evaluated population. During the study, some factors that are essential for building healthy competitions have been observed as missing from TIE, feedback and the lack of support from organizers to boost the learning opportunity that comes from participating. As is, TIE is a good student competition but is lacking in some areas which cause it to come short from the opportunity to provide students with a great learning opportunity, besides the possibility of winning a competition.

articleTitle: The conducted emission attenuations produced in the ON-GRID photovoltaic systems loaded with residential consumers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: It is already well known that the main source of electromagnetic interference produced by photovoltaic systems is generated by DC-DC and DC-AC converters. Although the means for attenuation of these unwanted emissions is well known, most photovoltaic power generation systems on the market still degrade the quality of the produced electrical energy, with reasons ranging from poor quality components of the system to the various range of consumer types. However, there is also a tendency to attribute the electromagnetic interferences generated by electric power generation systems in the residential sector only to the system itself, neglecting the influence of consumers. The research in this paper focused on measuring conduction emissions on the three phases of a residential building powered by a photovoltaic system. Various types of loads specific to the residential environment such as electric radiators, heat pumps, computers etc., were considered. The aim was to determine the frequency spectrum of these emissions and how they are influenced by the type of consumer. Another issue that has been investigated was whether conduction emissions are due to consumers, the inverter, or both.

articleTitle: An interactive visualization tool for circular economy and building materials recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Construction materials represent the largest material stock accumulated in modern society. The unprecedented growth of material stock is directly linked to high resource and energy consumption, demolition of waste discharges, and is correlated with the increased embodied energy and the associated CO2 emissions. Governments in Europe are looking for possibilities in the construction sector to replace raw materials with secondary resources through reuse and recycling by transitioning to a circular economy. But for cities, the practical aspects of the initiative remain challenging in multiple aspects. This work aims to introduce a visualization tool for built environment material stocks and flows to support circularity enabling recycling and reuse of these materials in existing buildings and infrastructures. The recovery of building materials in the circular economy requires map-based visualization tools through which statistical analyses can be made on buildings or groups of buildings. For this, it is necessary that the visualization tool contains API links to real building inventory data from local public authorities and advanced functions of real-time analysis of the attribute table and geospatial data.

articleTitle: TIE-M Plus: Alignment of Higher Education with Labor Market Demands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In the context of a constantly changing global economy, the relevance of higher education for labor market integration has a crucial impact. This article highlights the competencies acquired by students during their university studies and assesses how well they meet the requirements of industry employers. The research adopts a mixed approach, combining existing data with that obtained through the analysis of experiences of students participating in the TIE M Plus competition and the feedback received from employers. This reveals both strengths and deficiencies in university education, emphasizing the need to adapt the curriculum to better align with labor market demands. The TIE competition offers students the opportunity to put into practice the skills acquired during their university studies. The competition subjects are meticulously prepared by experts from leading companies, based on their direct expertise in the respective fields and a deep understanding of current market requirements and challenges. Solving and understanding these subjects is the best indicator of the preparation of future industry professionals. Therefore, the results obtained not only reflect their level of competence and ability to solve complex problems, but also demonstrate how well they are prepared to apply the skills acquired in university to meet the real world demands and challenges of the professional environment. To improve the alignment of higher education with labor market requirements, a close collaboration between higher education institutions and the business environment is necessary. Through this collaboration, major companies can provide real-time information on industry needs and can organize competitions like TIE in partnership, ensuring the relevance of university education and facilitating an efficient transition of graduates to the labor market.

articleTitle: On Calibration of the Magnetometer with the Help of the Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a method to calibrate the magnetometer. In practice the magnetometer is manufactured in the same chip among the gyroscope and the accelerometer. The magnetometer measures the magnetic field of the Earth. It is known that magnetic field has two parameters having values depending on the location on the Earth. These parameters are the magnitude and the angle to the horizon. It is presented a solution to rotate the magnetometer until its tri-dimensional output has a precise dependence to the two parameters of the magnetic field. This output is retained as a reference value. Then the magnetometer measurement is computed according to rotation matrix and this reference value. Rotation matrix depends on the gyroscope output. In this way, the magnetometer calibration is made simpler than the literature methods. The proposed method also eliminates soft iron and hard iron distortions because the gyroscope is not affected by such errors. Experimental results that confirms the proposed method, that are tested for two different sensors are presented.

articleTitle: A Blockchain Solution for Risk Management in Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents the use of a blockchain technology in risk management (B-RM) for the analysis of failure modes and effects (FMEA) as well as for the development of the control plan (CP) in the quality management system of an enterprise in the automotive field. The solution proposed by us substantially improves the risk assessment and management process through transparency, traceability and ensuring data integrity. At the same time, the implemented system improves the response speed of the parties involved. The study presents the solution proposed by us, how the system is implemented at the enterprise level, as well as some case studies in which the pilot model created by us was used. To validate our solution, performance comparisons were made with the classical solution that was applied in the enterprise. The results clearly show the benefits of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Designing Phase-Correction Sections Using an Active Implementation with an Operational Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper briefly presents the basic principles of phase correction. A model of a phase corrector using an active implementation with an op-amp is proposed. A methodology for its design is given in the paper. MATLAB program modules for the synthesis and analysis of phase correctors are developed. A MicroCAP simulation of the phase corrector designed using the suggested methodology is shown in the paper. A laboratory board is implemented for the study of amplitude and phase correctors according to the proposed methodology. The simulation results are compared with the experimental ones in the paper.

articleTitle: Concept and Challenges in Microcontroller Artificial Intelligence Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: There is a significant lag between the year a great idea is first proposed and the year it is eventually adopted and mainstreamed. The foundations of the Internet of Things (IoT) were introduced between 1960 and 1980, the concept was introduced in 1990, and its growth and expansion came after 2000. Proliferation and discussions on standardization were proposed after another 10 years. IoT evolution and development are tightly coupled to cloud-fog-edge architectures with the assumption that a significant amount of advanced processing occurs not on IoT devices but on clouds and fog. However, as the technology evolved, the required amount of data and connections indicated that previous ideas and concepts were not realistic and that data processing at the edge layer was required.

articleTitle: Sun Position Simulator for Solar Cell Testing and Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper describes a Sun position emulator. The design and implementation of the Sun position simulator is presented in the paper. A Sun position emulator is a very useful tool for research and education. A solar panel have a fixed position, but the Sun will have a daily trajectory from East to West. The elevation of the Sun in the middle of the day will vary from winter to summer. The optimal position, related to the Sun, of the photovoltaic panel can be determined with the proposed equipment. The position of the photovoltaic panel is very important in order to extract the maximum power from the photovoltaic panel.

articleTitle: The Development and Electrical and Morphological Characterization of some Electrodes on the Sponge Structure used in the Realization of Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The development of supercapacitor electrodes is an interesting topic in the development of structures for storing and generating electrical energy. The electrodes play a crucial role in terms of active surface area, amount of stored charge and are characterized by a number of electrical parameters, such as equivalent series resistance, electrical capacitance or electrical conductivity. In this work, we propose a new approach for the fabrication of electrodes on a nickel substrate and different types of kitchen sponges with different porosity. Electrodes with and without sponge are compared to emphasize the advantages of using kitchen sponges in the structure of the fabricated electrodes, as cheap, replaceable and biodegradable materials. Four electrodes were fabricated: one in which no sponge was usedand in which the material was applied directly to the nickel substrate with a roller and a current collector, and three other electrodes for which kitchen sponges with different porosity were used.

articleTitle: Investigating Optimal Feedback Functions of Second Degree for Nonlinear Feedback Shift Registers Using Computer-Based Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Nonlinear feedback shift registers (NLFSRs) are reliable tools for generating pseudorandom bits. Due to their efficiency and high security, NLFSRs are very important components in many security applications, such as network protocols and blockchains. NLFSRs are known to be more secure than linear feedback shift registers. However, it is difficult to obtain their optimal feedback functions due to the lack of a mathematical basis for NLFSRs. The paper presents computer-based tools for investigating optimal feedback functions of second degree for nonlinear feedback shift registers. The tools are used in the educational process in the course “Telecommunication Security” for the 7th-semester students in the specialty “Internet and Mobile Communications” at the University of Ruse “Angel Kanchev”.

articleTitle: Development of Automotive-mobility Training in the TRIREME project
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: To achieve climate neutrality by 2050, the consistent transformation of the mobility sector is one of the most important pillars of the European Green deal. As a result of green and sustainable approaches, novel automotive concepts and massive digitalisation in the mobility ecosystem is undergoing a continuous development towards eco-friendly solutions and novel business models, and the changing landscape of automotive industry comes with a significant social impact as well. The overall horizontal collaboration on skills agenda in the Automotive-Mobility Ecosystem is assured throughout the Automotive Skills Alliance (ASA) [1], which is the Large-scale Pact for Skills Partnership. The latest strategic project of the partnership to support its activities is the Digital & Green Skills Towards Future of the Mobility Ecosystem (TRIREME) which promotes a collaboration between industry stakeholders and training providers including Vocational education Trainings (VETs), Higher Educations (HEs) and universities), moreover, also emphasizing the widespread public representation of different project segments and evaluating the social impacts and regional impact of the changes in the Automotive-Mobility Ecosystem. In parallel to the development of sectoral skills strategy, our department (Department of Electronics Technology - ETT) is contributing to deliver specific training materials and courses within Work Package 4 (WP4), which is based on the gathered and processed intelligence from previous desk research, survey activity and participation in professional events. The methodology of course development relies on the concept of modularity, our professional competences in the field of Automotive-mobility, and the fulfillment of requirements to cover the needed skills, the competence and the occupational profile subsets.

articleTitle: Electronic Device Price Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to develop a software application that can forecast the price of a product using data collected from a database and present it in a web interface. This example demonstrates how the application accurately predicts the price of any electrical device based on its unique features and current pricing or price history. The application consists of four primary steps: database processing, machine learning training, exporting the model in a user interface, and making the prediction.

articleTitle: Influence of the Electrodes Porosity on the Supercapacitors’ Charging Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs) present moderate specific energy in comparison with batteries, which can be increased by structural modifications in the system electrodes - electrolytes. Porous electrodes variants offer possibility to control the phenomena in the Helmholtz layer (HL). Linear evolution of the electric potential in function of distance can be modified and accordingly the charge / discharge time. Different structural parameters have been considered in order to modify the potential in the HL, such as: ion size in the electrolyte, electrode surface area, electrolyte ionic conductivity, electrolyte viscosity. The electrolyte ionic conductivity depends on the number of charge carriers in the solution, ionic mobility, and valency of the ions. Carbon aerogels electrodes have been considered, with porosity of about 50 up to 80%. The HFSS program by Ansys was used for structural simulation, when the Molecular Dynamics method was applied for different NPT sceneries. By parameters correlation, an improvement of about 12% of the specific energy is expected when the phenomena in the Helmholtz layer are controlled.

articleTitle: IoT Devices for Monitoring and Analysing Air Quality in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents and air quality and UV monitoring IoT system suited for urban environments. The system consists of several IoT nodes, scattered around the monitored area, which are able to collect and report air quality and UV data to a central server. The gathered data is presented on an interactive color-coded map, which offers an overview of the conditions inside the monitored area. A mobile application is also offered through which users can monitor preferred areas or nodes.

articleTitle: A study on multi-modal LLM reasoning for defect detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In the modern landscape of manufacturing, the early and accurate detection of defects is pivotal to maintaining product quality and operational efficiency. This study investigates the application of multi-modal Large Language Models (LLMs) in enhancing defect detection processes. Leveraging the capabilities of LLMs to interpret diverse data types, such as text and visual imagery, this research explores how these models can provide comprehensive defect analysis, and how this analysis can be used for more than just detection. Through our experiments, we demonstrate that multi-modal LLMs have the potential to detect complex visual defects without any training, although with less accuracy and speed than trained convolutional neural network-based models. Moreover, the general context and text-based communication can be useful for deriving further analytics for the production process and for training purposes. On our ceramic defect dataset, the LLMs correctly detected, but not localized, between 10% and 33% of the defects present in the analyzed images, proving that large pre-training is very comprehensive versus a mean average precision (mAP@IoU 0.5) of 0.531 for a YOLO based model. The study also delves into the challenges of integrating different data modalities and the real time constraints of defect detection with are not yet solved with multimodal LLMs, while providing legal context.

articleTitle: Optimizing Power Consumption: A Comparative Analysis of Radio Modules used in Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Nowadays, power consumption is a critical topic in electronics due to the dynamic environment and the emphasis on green energy. This paper analyses the potential for reducing power consumption in embedded systems by selecting the appropriate radio module for the application. This method, related to the design phase of a system, is one of the techniques used to achieve power-aware design. In this paper five different radio modules are examined. These modules are commonly used in applications operating at 433 MHz. By comparing the results, we can choose the most suitable radio module based on power consumption, maximum distance, and the type of application.

articleTitle: Impact of Fe-NPs doped flux on electromigration in Sn-based solder joints of chip-sized SMD components at lower Joule heating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The influence of incorporating iron nanoparticles through flux doping (0-2wt.%) in lead-free SAC305 (Sn3.5Ag0.5Cu) solder joints of chip-sized surface-mounted (SMD) components on electromigration has been investigated. To ensure high current densities throughout the experiment, track-to-pad joining angles of 135° on the anode site and 90° on the cathode site were implemented. The temperature was kept relatively low to minimize material transport attributable to thermal effects. Microstructural changes were examined through cross-sectional analysis, and push-off shear tests were performed to assess the influence of current loading on mechanical reliability. After 2000 and 4000 h of loading the samples with 4 A, joints with 0402 resistors showed copper dissolution from the tracks at the cathode sites in samples prepared with undoped flux. However, among the NP doped samples, the joints produced with 0.5 wt.% Fe-NPs showed no copper dissolution. Shear performance of joints with 0402 components deteriorated in all cases after 4000 hours of current loading.

articleTitle: NLP-Based Solutions for Call Center Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Call center data flow processes audio recordings and text messages exchanged between clients and operators. Speech-to-text technology transcribes audio recordings into text. Modern call centers use Natural Language Processing (NLP) to process text messages and transcriptions, extracting keywords, named entities, or summarizing texts. This enables the system to update customer profiles, outline products, or identify frequently asked questions. The paper presents some results of processing audio data from a Romanian call center. We developed a subsystem to transcribe spoken customer messages and extract keywords and named entities. To build customer profiles, we extracted information such as names, phone numbers, address elements, and purchased product details. For product definitions, we considered names and, if available, product codes. We used Python, Google Speech-ToText API, and libraries like Spacy, Rake, T5, and scikit-learn. Despite challenges, we drew valuable conclusions.

articleTitle: Implementing of a New Software-Defined Radio Receiver Used for DSSS-CDMA Data Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper a new software-defined radio receiver used for DSSS-CDMA data signals is presented. The proposed radio receiver is intended for the reception of data signals with DSSS-CDMA modulation transmitted in the FM radio broadcasting infrastructure according to different scenarios of vehicular communications. For detecting of the data signal the circuit proposed in this paper is based on a carrier synchronization loop, operating at baseband and a DSSSCDMA demodulator. These stages are controlled by a symbol timing synchronization loop, which provides the maximum effect points (of both received DSSS-CDMA and DEQPSK signals) by using the Early Late timing error detector (ELTED) algorithm. The proposed circuit has been implemented in MATLAB/Simulink for an input data rate of $2375 \mathrm{bit} / \mathrm{s}$ and simulated under the conditions of different offset values of both carrier frequency and data rate on an AWGN communication channel, and also using an experimental setup that includes two USRP devices of type N210. In order to validate the simulation results, the bit error rate depending on signal-to-noise ratio of the radiofrequency DSSS-CDMA signal has been plotted for different communication scenarios.

articleTitle: Innovations in Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment: The Path Towards Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this work, we explore the main problems raised by Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE), crucial for the electric vehicle (EV) transition towards sustainable transportation. It explores the operational challenges, opportunities, and the role of EVSE in energy transition and environmental sustainability, addressing the environmental impacts of fossil fuel consumption. The utility of EVSE extends beyond electric vehicle charging, serving as a cornerstone for smart grid integration, demand response, and renewable energy utilization. Highlighting innovative applications in agriculture, the paper discusses how smart EVSE can optimize charging schedules, integrate with renewable energy sources, and facilitate the charging of autonomous farm machinery, enhancing grid stability and reducing operational costs. Moreover, it analyzes current technologies, regulatory frameworks trends and proposes new systems that aim to develop a sustainable transportation infrastructure, revolutionize agricultural operations and reduce the agricultural sector’s carbon footprint.

articleTitle: Assessment on measuring and estimation of Ragone plots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A synthetic mode to appreciate the capabilities of the energy storage technologies is represented by the diagram called Ragone plot after the author name and first introduction in 1968. The Ragone plot depicts the relationship between the energy that can be delivered from an energy storage device (e.g. battery or capacitor) and the discharge power. Although widely used, there are not many details about how the plots were obtained. We present a principle laboratory method for determination of Ragone plots for different energy storage systems, as supercapacitors or batteries. The experimental results are compared with calculated data, showing a relative good match.

articleTitle: Electronic Apiary Monitoring System with Built-in Sensors and Motorized Hive Access Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper focuses on the digitalization of beekeeping operations within an apiary, introducing an advanced monitoring system for multiple hives. The system is designed to collect and analyze essential data, such as temperature, relative humidity, hive mass, and internal sound intensity. Additionally, it incorporates a remote-controlled motor-operated door mechanism for hive entrance control. The monitoring system employs a complex setup to ensure effective data processing and display. The development process involves various stages, including schematic diagram conception, printed circuit design and manufacturing, assembling, and comprehensive testing, to ensure optimal performance in a real-life apiary setting.

articleTitle: IoT Beehive Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a system that represents an innovative approach to the management of beehives through the integration of modern technology. The system is designed to monitor various critical parameters within the hive and provide real-time feedback on its health and productivity. The novelty of this project lies in the use of a modular and open-source platform that utilizes wireless communication technologies for data acquisition and transmission and leverages the well-documented ESP32 development platform. This setup allows for a scalable and customizable solution that can be adapted to the specific needs of individual beekeepers. The main parameters to be monitored are temperature, humidity, hive weight, CO2 concentration and general hive monitoring. For use in remote areas, the system is equipped with a solar panel to utilize renewable energy, coupled with a battery management system that ensures the sustainability and reliability of the system. The main achievement of this project is the creation of a user-friendly and efficient monitoring platform that can significantly improve the users’ experience, guiding them to make better management decisions for the hive. In summary, the Beehive Monitoring System is a practical and innovative solution for small and medium sized beekeepers that combines modern technology with the basic requirements of hive management, providing a powerful tool to improve the sustainability of bee colonies.

articleTitle: Intelligent Emergency Braking System for Bicycle
