publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative emergency braking system designed to enhance the safety of children on bicycles. The system allows remote braking control by an adult, reducing the risk of accidents and promoting safer rides. The system consists of a transmitter and a receiver, utilizing two Arduino Nano boards and two NRF24L01+ wireless modules. The novelty of this project lies in the real-time control of braking, using a joystick to send braking commands, which are transmitted wirelessly to the receiver. The receiver then activates a servomotor connected to the bicycle’s braking system. This remote control provides parents with the ability to intervene immediately in emergency situations, thus contributing to the child’s safety. Furthermore, the system’s compact design, powered by LiPo batteries, ensures portability and reliability in comparison to traditional braking systems.

articleTitle: Haptic system for the remote control of a robotic structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Robot teleoperation is a transformative field that can enable workers to safely perform tasks in dangerous environments [1]. This paper presents the development of an independent control system, capable of acquiring and providing haptic feedback, whilst uploading real-time data to a Wi-Fi connected database. The chosen control method is presented and concurrently optimized through the implementation of a simplistic sample fusion algorithm. The implemented feedback subsystem provides the dimension of the gripped object. Simultaneously, as an automated system, a safety subsystem has been implemented that stops the entire control process and alerts the operator upon detecting an obstruction within the robotic manipulator’s workspace. This research highlights the impact of the implemented data processing algorithms on both the responsiveness and accuracy of the system, proposing methods to optimize its overall performance.

articleTitle: Integration of UHF RFID Receptors in Railway Maintenance Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper discusses the deployment of UHF RFID receptors equipped with various sensors to enhance the maintenance of railway infrastructure. These receptors provide continuous, real-time data on safety parameters, addressing the challenge of limited revision times in subway systems. Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are emphasized for their cost-effectiveness, high resolution, robustness, and low power consumption. WSNs consist of small-scale sensors capable of data processing and communication, offering advantages like self-organization, short-range broadcasting, dense deployment, and continuous topology changes. Effective management of these networks involves addressing energy consumption, data transmission, and signal processing to ensure stability and efficiency. The proposed system utilizes UHF RFID receptors, RFID tags and infrared sensors to monitor rail integrity and environmental conditions. Data is centrally processed and transmitted via GSM with GPS positioning for real-time event localization. The study examines energy consumption, distance measurement, and information transmission delays, proposing the deployment of WSNs in UHF RFID receptors to improve railway safety. Potential applications extend to civilian, military, and emergency response contexts.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Magnetic Interaction between Atoms using a Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The main goal of the analysis carried out in this paper was to establish the best algorithm among four neural network algorithms chosen to approach and solve the problem of predicting scalar coupling constants between two atoms within the same molecule. It will be shown that the most important aspect of the analyzed deep neural network is related to the input features on which the training is done.

articleTitle: Characterizing Thermal Properties of 18650 Lithium-Ion Battery Cells: Experimental Approaches to Thermal Conductivity and Specific Heat Capacity Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive experimental analysis of the thermal parameters of cylindrical 18650 lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery cells, focusing on thermal conductivity and specific heat capacity. Using a controlled heat source provided by a Peltier module and measuring and recording the temperatures on both ends of the battery cells, this research investigates how varying heat input rates affect these critical thermal properties. The experiments were conducted on several types of battery cells to compare the effects of different chemistries and structural designs on thermal behavior. The findings reveal variations in how these batteries conduct and store heat, highlighting the influence of increased power inputs on enhancing thermal conductivity. These results contribute to a better understanding of battery performance under different operational stresses and provide valuable insights for optimizing battery design and safety in applications where thermal management is crucial.

articleTitle: Algorithms for Processing Signals of Alcohol Consumption Detecting Sensors And Engine Control Interface In Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The main purpose of this system is to detect drivers who have consumed alcoholic beverages and if the sensor detects alcohol vapors to block the vehicle’s engine. Mainly, the system is composed of two subsystems: one for detecting the alcohol vapors of the person sitting behind the wheel and one for validating the start of the engine. The alcohol vapor detection system registers alcohol vapors with the help of a sensor placed in the axial direction of the driver’s breath to detect alcohol. The analog signal is sent to the microcontroller system, this through the input converter, it is analyzed and through the CAN network it validates or not the engine start and a numerical message is displayed on the LCD screen. In parallel, a message is displayed by turning on the green LED when a zero or very low concentration of alcohol is measured, yellow for a medium concentration and red for a high concentration of alcohol. Also, at a high concentration of alcohol, the system used will command, by means of a high-current relay, the blocking of the engine start system and, in parallel, the triggering of a buzzer warning sound of an alarm sound signal. When the source of alcohol is removed, after 10 seconds it unlocks the vehicle’s starting device and the engine can be started if the other conditions are met: The system stops the engine if it detects the presence of the signal from the alcohol sensor or from the video or tactile driver fatigue system on the steering wheel

articleTitle: On the Forgetting Factors of the RLS Algorithm Based on Third-Order Tensor Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The recently developed recursive least-squares algorithm based on third-order tensor decomposition, namely RLSTOT, proves to be efficient for the identification of long length impulse responses. Such systems can be encountered in many real-world applications, like network/acoustic echo cancellation. The RLS-TOT combines the estimates of three shorter adaptive filters, which have different convergence parameters. In this paper, we investigate some strategies for setting the forgetting factors of the RLS-TOT. These are the main parameters that control the memory of the algorithm and, consequently, its main performance criteria. Simulations performed in the framework of echo cancellation support the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Thermal Simulations and Characterization of High-Power LED Boards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: High-power light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are pivotal in modern lighting applications, especially in automotive systems. However, thermal management remains a critical challenge, hence this study focuses on thermal simulation and characterization of high-power LED boards to optimize thermal design and enhance reliability. We employed computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model heat dissipation mechanisms in LED assemblies, considering various placements for the components in case of natural cooling. Key parameters, including junction temperature and thermal distribution, were evaluated. This study underscores the importance of integrated thermal management solutions in high-power LED systems and provides a robust framework for future design improvements.

articleTitle: Increasing the Specific Energy of Environmental Friendly EDLC and Pseudocapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The electrochemical storage mechanism of the electrical energy in the (electrical double layer capacitor) EDLC and respectively peseudocapacitors was studied, based on the Gouy-Chapman-Stern model. Our target is represented by the biodegradable materials for pseudocapscitors’ synthesis. In order to improve the specific energy accumulated inside the structures, a correlation between structural parameters is necessary, which can be identified by simulation methods. The HFSS program was used and Molecular Dynamics method was applied to describe the ions dynamics inside the structure, where non-faradaic and faradaic charge transfer occur. For a particular set of environmental friendly materials, the capacitance - voltage - current density dependences were pointed out, in order to illustrate the particularities of the phenomena. Materials for electrodes cellulose derivatives or based on the poly(3-hydroxybutyrrate) (PHB) natural polymer, in association with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) biodegradable electrolyte do not perform very high charge accumulation, in comparison with other types of non-biodegradable materials, but their performance can be improved from about 20 to 26-36 $\mu \mathrm{F} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$. Ions’ properties were correlated with the electrodes porosity and salt concentration of the electrolyte, for current maximal densities around $25 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{g}$. The analysis method can be applied for different type of materials, considering their structural properties and mutual interaction forces.

articleTitle: Comparative Workbench Study of MTBF for PoL Converters with discrete Transistors vs. integrated PoL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Designers of power supplies (intended for any type of load) have recently been making efforts to increase their reliability and efficiency. This is imperatively required by the current Decarbonization concept which imposes design restrictions on energy consumption, materials and maintenance. A new trend that is part of these wishes is the use of IPoL (Integrated Point of Load) DC-DC converters. The novelty brought by this work is the comparison of the figures obtained for the reliability prediction of a PoL DC-DC converter made with discrete devices vs. an integrated one. Finally, it is established that the integrated converter has a higher reliability.

articleTitle: Resistive and Capacitive Sensors Driver for Irrigation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Following the climate changes of today, high summer temperatures accompanied by dry air have become more frequent in Romania. This is a direct factor which influences the agriculture field in the entire country, by changing the resilience of plants and crops. To overcome some of the problems, an automated irrigation system is essential. To achieve high efficiency of the irrigation system, the watering is set based on the soil humidity. An array of humidity (resistive or capacitive) sensors is installed on the working field, to gather the mean humidity of the fields soil. The main control unit consists of several analogue circuits for averaging humidities, setting references, controlling the water pump, ensuring safety and setting the user interface. The system provides a reliable and easy to use solution for farmers, to automate the irrigation process.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Electroencephalogram (EEG) Signals Using Pre-Amplification and Filtering Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The primary goal of this study is to provide students with practical experience in measuring and analyzing electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. This involves understanding the effects of visual stimulation on alpha wave activity and managing interference signals to ensure accurate recordings. The human brain’s cortex contains numerous neurons that can synchronize, resulting in rhythmic behaviors detectable as electrical signals on the scalp. These signals, known as EEGs, are crucial for studying brain activity and diagnosing neurological conditions. Different states of alertness and external stimuli affect these signals, which can be categorized into delta, theta, alpha, and beta waves based on their frequency.

articleTitle: Advanced Electronics System for the Improvement of Concrete Factories Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The electronic system, designed for a concrete factory, addresses the challenge of maintaining continuous production by monitoring the levels of cement powder and additives. This system employs radar sensors to gather real-time data of materials, which is then displayed for the factory management to assess the current situation. By implementing this electronic solution, the factory can prevent production halts caused by low material levels, ensuring a smooth and efficient manufacturing process. The innovative scientific approach of using radar sensors for data collection provides accurate and reliable information, enabling the factory to make informed decisions and maintain optimal production levels. Additionally, the system’s architecture allows for scalability and integration with existing industrial automation frameworks, enhancing process oversight and facilitating proactive maintenance strategies that further bolster operational reliability and cost-efficiency.

articleTitle: Dynamic Adaptation Algorithm of LoRa Communication Parameters in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: LoRa, an acronym for “Long Range” communication protocol, gained great popularity to be used in wireless sensor networks (WSN). The main advantage of this protocol is the reduced energy consumption for long-range data transmission. To make energy consumption more efficient a series of communication parameters must be adapted accordingly. This paper presents a dynamic adaptation algorithm that uses Spreading Factor, Coding Rate, Bandwidth, and Transmission Power to reduce packet errors with minimum energy consumption based on the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI). Tests were made using a point-to-point scenario with a custom wireless sensor node for environmental data acquisition.

articleTitle: TIE T+- Thermal Management Student Contest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This article introduces the TIE-Thermal Plus student contest, which builds on the TIE framework by focusing on the main aspect of managing heat in electronics. Effective thermal management is vital for the performance, reliability, and lifetime of electronic components. By keeping devices within safe temperature limits, we can prevent overheating and failures. The article explores different methods for managing heat, such as using different emissivity of material, and cooling systems under natural and forced convection. This explains why these are important for keeping electronics running smoothly. The contest encourages students to create and apply innovative thermal management solutions, helping them gain practical experience with real-world problems in the electronics industry. The TIE-Thermal Plus contest expands the TIE framework and highlights the essential role of good thermal practices in the success of electronic devices.

articleTitle: Numerical Measurement System of Fluid Flows in Pipelines Without Affecting the Integrity of the Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The basic principle for measuring flow without interfering with the integrity of the pipe through which a fluid flows is the ultrasonic propagation in fluids. The central device of the system is a transducer and consists of an ultrasound transmitter, a receiver made of piezoceramic material and an electronic circuit with a microcontroller for signal processing. Such a device consists of an ultrasonic signal generator with variable frequency, which excites a piezo-ceramic actuator fixed on the outside of the pipe. The actuator emits mechanical oscillations that propagate in the fluid flowing through the pipe. Similarly, a piezoelectric element is placed on the pipe as a sensor that receives the ultrasonic oscillations propagated through the fluid and transforms them into an electrical signal. The processing of the received signal is analyzed and compared with the emitted signal from the point of view of time delays in relation to the excitation signal, the variations of some parameters that depend on the fluid flow rate, respectively on its flow rate through the closed pipe, can be highlighted

articleTitle: New Evaluation for Thermal Diffusivity of High-Power Devices with Different Packages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The high voltage and low loss power electronic devices of the future are based on silicon carbide (SiC), which is a wide-bandgap compound semiconductor with superior physical and electrical properties over silicon (Si). The on-state resistance of some SiC power devices is orders of magnitude lower (for example, seven times lower in this paper) than that of silicon devices at a given blocking voltage. This paper presents a thermal comparison for several power devices, with different packages and ON resistances, based on a key thermal transport parameter, the thermal diffusivity. Investigations for this work were conducted using a new method for the measurement of thermal diffusivity.

articleTitle: Education 5.0: Transforming Engineering Education in the Age of Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The rise of generative AI is reshaping the landscape of Higher Education with implications we must understand and be prepared for. A future engineering graduate that fulfills the Industry 5.0 requirements must demonstrate proficiency in a range of competencies, including innovation, artificial intelligence (AI) methods, creativity, AI-supported decision-making, complex problem solving and leadership. This paper presents three case studies for developing future skills in Engineering Education for Industry 5.0 using problem-based learning, scenario-based learning and non-traditional laboratories that integrate generative AI in their teaching approaches. They were developed to increase students, motivation, curiosity, self-reflection, collaboration, hands-on and multiple perspective thinking of academic learning and new strategies to achieve established goals. Furthermore, the integration of generative AI, GNU Radio, powered GPUs represents a significant advance in radio transceiver development. This synergy boosts the performance and adaptability of radio systems, fostering new research and innovation opportunities in wireless communications.

articleTitle: Enclosure with Underground Passive Cooling System for High Power Vehicle Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents the approach to designing the electrical casing with a passive cooling system for a high-power charging station. Fast-charging stations of 50 kW need to be installed in various locations in Germany. It is challenging to install such systems in congested areas as this system together with its components and cooling system requires large spaces. Thus, it is proposed to be installed under the ground of parking lots with dispensing units available over the ground. Passive cooling systems play a vital role in maintaining the efficiency. It saves the energy required for a fan or liquid circulation in active cooling. In this case, it is not possible to use natural convection for passive cooling therefore geothermal cooling is considered. The idea is that at a depth of 2 m to 4 m under the ground temperature remains constant at around $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ throughout the year. Thus, the casing is designed to dissipate around 500 W of heat from the electrical components mounted on heatsinks in contact with soil. Soil plays a major role in heat dissipation underground. In general soil thermal conductivity is low therefore large surface area-to-heat ratio is required to dissipate the heat. For design basis, two experiments are performed to know, the behavior of local soil and thermal conductivity. In the former experiment, the temperature of the soil at 2 m depth is recorded, and later the thermal conductivity is evaluated for dry and moist soil resulting in 1.8 to $2.0 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{m}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Other parameters such as heat from each component, even heat distribution and weather conditions are also considered. Transient thermal simulation is performed to analyse the design resulting in a temperature of $66^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in 16 hours of heat application. Based on simulation results casing is manufactured and tested in real conditions resulting in a maximum temperature of $56^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in 16 hours. Thus, it provides a suitable temperature for the working of electrical components.

articleTitle: Advancing Forest Conservation: IoT Devices for Monitoring the Wellbeing of Ecosystems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper proposes and IoT monitoring system that is able to detect and alert the competent authorities when illegal activities (such as deforestation or poaching) occur inside of protected forests, as well as establish an early alert system in case of forest fires. The monitoring system relies on a series of solar powered IoT nodes, which can connect to each other and transmit information from deep inside forests where data coverage may not be available.

articleTitle: AI Tools introduced in Software Development. Analysis of Code quality, Security and Productivity Implications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Chatbots have recently been integrated into a diverse range of applications, from office tools to code compilers. It is undeniable that AI assistants possess features that simplify and automate repetitive tasks, however, it is yet unclear how well they can handle creative tasks such as writing code. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the quality of the solutions generated by AI tools, that have been specifically trained for software development tasks, including code writing, testing, reviewing and documenting features. Individual use cases are rigorously examined, while comparing the results for two similar intelligent assistants per each scenario, to identify the strengths and weaknesses of their proposed solutions. The impact on productivity is studied, as it is dependent on the quality of the generated responses. The implementation of an incomplete, outdated or insecure solution will impose additional fixes, and, if the majority of answers have to be revised, this counterproductive behavior will actually increase the development time rather than facilitate its reduction.

articleTitle: Intelligent System for Integration in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This study investigates the performance and resilience of 5 G networks through an experimental setup based on 3GPP standards, employing Open5GS and srsRAN software. A baseline for normal network operations was established, with key metrics including channel quality indicators (CQI) and bitrates, followed by the introduction of controlled jamming to assess network disruptions. The network’s response to these disruptions was analyzed using a Random Forest (RF) algorithm, which demonstrated perfect accuracy in distinguishing between normal and jamming states. The results underscore the potential of 5 G technology in applications requiring low latency and high reliability, such as autonomous vehicles and remote surgeries. Furthermore, the study explores security implications and future advancements in edge computing and network slicing, contributing to a deeper understanding of 5G networks’ capabilities and vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Knowledge in Test Engineering Education using a Solar-powered Remote-controlled Flying Probe-Inspired In-Circuit Tester
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a solar-powered remote-controlled Flying Probe-Inspired In-Circuit Tester (FPICT) designed to improve individuals’ knowledge and practical skills in the Test Engineering Education (TEE) domain. The proposed system consists of a user-friendly modern website that offers three main functions: (a) access to TEE-related documentation and tests, (b) a real-time webcam feed for remote monitoring, access, control, and execution of real-time tests on multiple Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) using the FPICT platform, and (c) performance assessment of users’ TEE knowledge improvement. The effectiveness of the FPICT in enhancing TEE knowledge is evaluated by comparing the score distribution of users before and after the initial tests. Additionally, the power consumption of the FPICT platform is measured, and the feasibility of powering the system with solar energy is investigated. Experimental results demonstrate that the remote-controlled FPICT successfully increases the TEE-related knowledge of web users by an average of $26 \%$ over an average duration of 50 minutes, highlighting its efficacy in teaching theoretical concepts of In-Circuit Testing (ICT) and developing practical skills in the Flying Probe Testing (FPT) domain.

articleTitle: Optimal energy management for an islanded microgrid with battery degradation cost considerations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing focus on the role of battery energy storage systems in diverse applications within power systems. As the charging and discharging of batteries is closely tied to cell degradation, improper usage can significantly reduce the battery’s lifespan. For the optimal functioning of islanded microgrids with integrated energy storage systems, when both economic and functional considerations are taken into account, accurately determining and integrating battery degradation costs into the energy management problem is crucial. This study explores three distinct methods for calculating battery degradation costs and successfully integrates them into the optimal scheduling problem of an islanded microgrid. This approach not only prioritizes the efficient use of batteries but also ensures the microgrid operates with optimal parameters. The results obtained from these methodologies are compared, leading to valuable insights.

articleTitle: Decision support prototype for farmers based on environmental parameter modelling through supervised machine learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Supervised machine learning models are increasingly prevalent across a wide range of domains. Farming, a fundamental means of subsistence throughout human history, is no exception. Consequently, machine learning algorithms have emerged as valuable tools for the monitoring and management of crops. This paper provides a comparative analysis of predicting soil temperature based on air parameters using various supervised machine learning techniques, including Linear Regression, Decision Trees and Ensemble Learning. Using this, farmers can extract accurate soil temperature forecasts through a newly developed intuitive graphical user interface (GUI), enhancing their ability to make informed agricultural decisions.

articleTitle: Small-Scale V2V-VLC for Enhanced Road Traffic Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In the context of global research aimed at enhancing data transfer rates and efficiency, light emerges as a cost-free and unregulated asset that has the potential to revolutionize communication technologies. The complete replacement of conventional lighting with LEDs led to the development of a novel optical communication system. Visible light communication (VLC) uses LEDs as transmitters and photodetectors or image sensors as receivers. The technology has significant potential for a range of applications, especially in intelligent transport systems (ITS). In this context, the headlights and taillights of vehicles can transmit different types of information to other vehicles, enhancing traffic safety and ultimately preventing fatalities on the road. The paper proposes a small-scale vehicle-to-vehicle ITS that uses robot-type cars that are equipped with emission and reception modules. The cars transmit various information using VLC to implement a variety of events, including emergency braking, deceleration, left or right turns, and engine on/off, all of which are essential for road traffic safety. The maximum distance between vehicles that ensures successful data transmission will also be determined.

articleTitle: Automated Greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper proposes the development of an automated greenhouse system along with a method for controlling and monitoring essential parameters. The system consists of an ATmega64A microcontroller embedded on a PCB (Printed Circuit Board), five sensors, two control components, and a Wi-Fi module. To ensure the protection of sensitive components, galvanic isolation was implemented, separating external connections from those on the 4-layer PCB. Communication between the ATmega64A and ThingsBoard, an open-source Internet of Things platform, is facilitated by the Wi-Fi module using the MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) protocol. A Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy inference system is employed to calculate water flow based on air temperature and soil humidity. While this solution is similar to existing market options, it offers a cost-effective, user-friendly control system and data logging that is accessible from anywhere at any time.

articleTitle: Advanced Collaboration in the Romanian Electronics Field based on the TIE Professional Student Contest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In the Romanian electronics field, one of the main results of the partnership between academia and industry is the TIE (renamed TIE-E) Professional Student Contest. This partnership result aims to challenge the students, year after year, to develop their abilities in CAD techniques for development of printed circuits (PCB) and electronic modules. The entire process, from designing a component with symbol and footprint, to an entire PCB with a lot of constraints and design rules, followed by the necessary fabrication files, is emphasized with this contest. Best $30 \cdots 40$ students from Romanian universities, and not only, are welcomed every year to solve the difficult tasks developed by industry and academia. The contest’s subjects are annually updated to reflect the latest technological advancements in the industry. In this context, the paper presents a general description and information related to TIE-E and is a detailed walk through the 2024 contest subject.

articleTitle: Comparing large language model artificial intelligence tools in aid of electrical engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Conversational AI (artificial intelligence) systems have broken into the digital technology sphere at the end of 2022. Many scientists, engineers, and authors have begun using them despite a lack of evidence for their applicability. Research has been conducted in several fields, including electrical engineering, on the applicability of generative AI in many fields, such as chemical engineering, programming, medicine, and even electrical engineering. Most, although not all, of the existing research focuses on applying specific AI models. This case study compares several generative AI models (ChatGPT, Bard, Bing AI, Copilot) through tasks in electrical engineering design. We qualitatively evaluated the AI responses to the questions. We have found that although AI tools are applicable and perform similarly well in general questions, their use is highly questionable in more specific cases, for example, in circuit design. Lastly, AIs perform equally unacceptably in tasks that require specific data, such as literature reviews. We conclude that the bots should be used sparingly with strict supervision and professional knowledge.

articleTitle: Stand for testing the lifetime of an automotive electronic module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a solution for creating a life time test stand, LTT (Life Time Tester), for an automotive electronic module, mounted on a vehicle. The requirements based on which the stand architecture was designed and the motivation for choosing the hardware components are presented. The software resources were chosen to enable the implementation and validation of automated test sequences. The specificity of testing the operation in extreme conditions led to the use of a multithreading structure for the implementation of the test sequences. The method of processing the results and generating the test reports followed the requirements of the standards.

articleTitle: SIMD Extensions - A Historical Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This work provides a historical perspective on the Single Instruction Multiple Data (SIMD) instruction set extensions. SIMD extensions are crucial in modern processors for handling large amounts of data and exploiting data-level parallelism. The effectiveness of SIMD optimizations is influenced by several factors, including data size. Modern SIMD extensions support both integer and floating point numbers. Furthermore, sub-word parallelism is exploited, improving performance when processing narrow data types. We provide an overview of the SIMD extensions for SPARC (VIS), x86 (MMX, SSE, AVX, AVX2, AVX-512, AMX), PowerPC (AltiVec), MIPS (MDMX), Arm (Neon, SVE, SVE2, SME) and RISC-V (RVV) architectures. Furthermore, we provide examples of modern processors featuring SIMD extensions for x86, Arm and RISC-V architectures.

articleTitle: Master-Slave BMS Architecture with CAN-bus for Inter-Cell Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, a Battery Management System (BMS) is designed and implemented to enable fast balancing of a 4S1P battery pack, which contains four Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) cells connected in series. The proposed Master-Slave architecture supposes a single Master node and four Slave nodes which communicate using a Controller Area Network (CAN). The Master node receives the measured parameters (voltage, temperature, balancing state) from all Slave nodes, detects if the battery pack is charged, compares the cells voltages, takes the decision which cell to be balanced, and transmits the balancing command to a specific Slave node. Also, the Master node has the role of protection for undervoltage, overvoltage, and overtemperature, by disabling the battery charger or the load. Each Slave node acquires cell data and enables passive balancing of that cell using high power resistors. The measured parameters and the operating states of the BMS can be also transmitted through the CAN-bus to other Electronic Control Units (ECUs), for example an LCD display.

articleTitle: TIE Micro – Chiplets and Next-gen Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: As the semiconductor industry advances towards heterogeneous integrations and sophisticated Systems in Package and chiplet technologies, it becomes imperative to equip future engineers with expertise in state-of-the-art methodologies, including the application of interposers, 2.5D and 3D integration. To address this need within the roadmap of the extracurricular education for future engineers, starting in 2024, the Technologies of Interconnections in Electronics (TIE) student competition introduced a new topic - TIE Micro (TIE-$\mu$), which focuses on advanced packaging. Participants are provided with the project topics in advance and are required to submit comprehensive project design files and a detailed project report. The report must explain the student’s methodological approach, the layout design, and the results from the signal and power integrity simulations. The top ranked students present their work through an oral presentation. The jury is comprised of academia and industry representatives.

articleTitle: Automated Control System for Photovoltaic Panel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents an automatic control system to achieve maximum energy efficiency from a solar panel. The proposed implementation integrates the power part and the orientation part into a single control module. The orientation part uses a mechanism with stepper motors to allow the solar panel to be positioned in the direction of the incident radiation. The power part consists of a synchronous buck converter, controlled in a closed loop, connected to a 12 V battery. A constant current - constant voltage charging cycle will be implemented, and an algorithm for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) will also be integrated into this process. To evaluate the performance of the converter, the SIMULINK program was used for testing the digital proportional-integral (PI) control, measuring the characteristic parameters, comparing the perturb and observe (P&O) and incremental conductance (IC) algorithms, and testing the charging cycle.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Analysis on eMMC Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 30th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper highlights the importance of signal integrity (SI) in modern high-speed circuits, focusing on maintaining signal quality in Printed Circuit Boards. Key SI challenges include managing signal reflections, overshoot, and crosstalk, essential for devices operating at high frequencies. The study addresses both time domain and frequency domain analyses, using parameters like eye diagrams and scattering parameters to evaluate channel performance. Implementation involves optimizing signal paths, trace widths, and via transitions between a high-performance System-on-Module and an Embedded Multi-Media Card memory, with careful attention to timing requirements. Using tools like HyperLynx, the study performs pre- and post-layout analyses to ensure proper signal integrity. Results demonstrate low signal reflection and crosstalk, validating the effectiveness of the design strategies employed.
